claim_summary: BRIDGE contributes an LLM multi-agent procedure that refines time-series descriptions into paired training data for text-controlled time-series generation, alongside a separate diffusion generator.

claim_evidence.quote: propose a novel LLM-based Multi-Agent framework that synthesizes diverse, realistic text-to-TS datasets.

modules.name: ReAct-based time-series template collection
modules.scope_reason: R3 selects GH: query decomposition and web-search execution are not bound to a task-family output criterion, and the module does not enforce temporal order, windows, frequency, units, or availability. Changing the downstream task leaves the search workflow intact, so neither TSK nor GTS applies.
rubric_path: R3_2_GTS:no - no temporal state or availability constraint
R3_3_GH:yes - general search and execution workflow

evidence.quote: we propose a single-agent framework, which prompts LLMs to generate dynamic reasoning traces for collecting candidates and actions to interact with external environments (e.g., Google, Wikipedia) in an interleaved manner

modules.name: Multi-agent description refinement for synthesis data
modules.scope_reason: R3 selects TSK because the refinement procedure evaluates text paired with a historical series through forecast performance; changing that task-specific verifier requires redesigning its evaluation objective. It is not a general temporal utility separable from that criterion, so GTS does not apply.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - refinement is evaluated against a forecasting criterion

evidence.quote: This is achieved by incorporating a ts task conditioned on accompanying text, based on the premise that higher-quality text improves performance.
we use LSTPrompt (Liu et al., 2024b) and LLMTime (Gruver et al., 2023) as our evaluation backbone

task_performance.quote: we use the Mean Absolute Error (MAE). For TCTSG, we measure the Marginal Distribution Discrepancy (MDD) and Kullback-Leibler (K-L) divergence to quantify the realism of the synthesized data

changes: dimensions: Control, Verification, and Feedback -> Planning and Orchestration; Coordination and Scaling -> Planning and Orchestration, Optimization and Evolution
reconciliation.reason: The packet supports the existing iterative multi-agent text-refinement mechanism and ties its evaluation to time-series forecasting performance; the new labels follow the current vocabulary.

The packet's diffusion generator is a method contribution, but its new mechanism is in the diffusion model and uses a pretrained LLM encoder unchanged. It neither modifies LLM-side temporal capability nor contributes a harness mechanism under R2.

notes: The packet does not report an experiment testing chronological split integrity, information cutoffs, or temporal leakage. The described external-source restriction is a data-preparation precaution, not an evaluated temporal-validity result. The added web-template collection mechanism is independently specified in the packet and supports the dataset construction contribution.
